headline: Approved $678,550 Teamsters contract funding, $1,158,400 non-union pay raise, Pelham Road easements, and several street resurfacing projects; denied 1432 Main Street rezoning.
summary: The council held public hearings on special permits for 220 Moody Street and 96 Tower Road, continuing both to October dates, and approved a street opening permit for Nicholas DiDuca at 20 Gale Street. It approved funding for a Teamsters union contract, a non-union employee pay raise, infrastructure and equipment purchases, two Pelham Road easements, and resurfacing on several streets. It also approved naming part of 617 Lexington Street for Robert Eagle, denied renaming it for John Daddona, denied a zoning change at 1432 Main Street, and withdrew a zoning amendment at 181-185 Felton Street.
decisions: Continued the special permit hearing for MICOL LLC at 220 Moody Street to October 26, 2026.
Continued the special permit hearing for CAVA Group, Inc. at 96 Tower Road to October 13, 2026.

Approved the 17-80 resurfacing of Kenmore Road, amended to include Kenmore Terrace, 12-0-0-2-1.

Approved the 17-80 resurfacing of Milner Street, 12-0-0-2-1.

1
Waltham City Council 
Minutes of the Meeting of 
August 3, 2026
President Logan called the meeting to order at 7:30 p.m. 
 
Artie Kronenfeld and Charlie Johnson from the Waltham Times were recognized as recording the 
meeting.
Present: Bradley-MacArthur, Dunn, Durkee, Harris, Hanley, Katz, King, LaFauci, LeBlanc, 
McLaughlin, Tzioumis, Vidal and President Logan. 
Absent: Brasco, LaCava.
City Clerk Vizard recited the Council Prayer followed by President Logan leading all present in the 
Pledge of Allegiance. Councillor Durkee asked for a moment of silence for all the military that have
served past and present. 
Councillor LeBlanc moved approval of the regular City Council meeting minutes of June 22, 2026. 
The motion was approved by a voice vote. 
Clerk Vizard read Rule 86.
First Public Hearing: Special Permit for MICOL LLC at 220 Moody Street (recessed 5/26/26)
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Attorney Phillip McCourt of 272 Bacon Street, 
Waltham, MA representing the petitioner, spoke on the matter explaining that all information 
requested from Committee would be provided in the next few weeks. With no one else in favor, 
no one else in opposition and no one in a neutral position to the zoning amendment President 
Logan closed that part of the public hearing and opened the hearing up to questions from 
Councillors. Councillor Harris made a motion that was approved by a voice vote to recess the 
hearing until a date certain of Monday, October 26, 2026.
Second Public Hearing: Special Permit for CAVA Group, Inc. at 96 Tower Road
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Attorney Michael Connors of 689 Main Street, 
Waltham, MA, Matthew Pelletier of BKA Architects, Quincy, MA and Nick Skoly of 101 Walnut 
Street, Watertown, MA all representing the petitioner, spoke on the matter. Five people stood in 
favor of the petition. With no one else in favor, no one in opposition and no one in a neutral position 
to the petition, President Logan closed that part of the public hearing and opened the hearing up to 
questions from Councillors. Councillors LaFauci, Bradley-MacArthur and Harris asked questions. 
Attorney Connors, Mr. Pelletier and Mr. Skoly provided answers. With no further questions 
Councillor Harris made a motion that was approved by a voice vote to recess the hearing until a date 
certain of Tuesday, October 13, 2026. President Logan referred the matter to the Ordinances and 
Rules Committee.
Third Public Hearing: 17-25 Street Opening at 20 Gale Street for Nicholas DiDuca
Clerk Vizard read the public hearing notice. Nicholas DiDuca of 110 Albert Road, Newton, MA the 
petitioner, spoke on the matter. Clerk Vizard read a communication in favor of the petition from 
Councillor LaCava. With no one else in favor, no one in opposition and no one in a neutral position 
to the petition President Logan closed that part of the public hearing and opened the hearing up to 
questions from Councillors. Councillors Hanley and LaFauci asked questions. Mr. DiDuca provided 
answers. With no further questions President Logan closed the public hearing and referred the matter
to the Public Works and Public Safety Committee.
2
Communications from the Mayor
1. The Mayor respectfully requested acceptance of statement of objections regarding veto of 
Order #s 36946 and 36947. Referred to the Ordinances and Rules Committee.
2. The Mayor respectfully requested acceptance pursuant to the provisions of City Ordinance
17-19, a request to name the west wing of 617 Lexington Street for Robert Eagle. Referred
to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
3. The Mayor respectfully requested a funding transfer totaling $678,550 to fund the first 
year and second year of a three-year collective bargaining agreement between the city and 
the Teamsters (Laborers) union for the period July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2028. Referred to 
the Finance Committee.
4. The Mayor respectfully requested acceptance of a donation to the Waltham Fire 
Department from the Revvity Foundation in the amount of $1,000. Referred to the Finance
Committee.
5. The Mayor respectfully requested the acceptance of the draft for the Cardinal Cottage 
affordable housing application package. The required Affordable Housing Restriction is 
being drafted by the Law Department. Referred to the Committee of the Whole.
6. The Mayor respectfully requested the confirmation of the appointment of Debra 
Catalanotti of 47 Lura Lane, Waltham as a permanent member of the Waltham Council on
Aging to fill a vacancy. Referred to the Committee of the Whole.
7. The Mayor respectfully requested the confirmation of the appointment of Diane Lane at 
152 Clark Lane, Waltham as a member of the Board of Cemetery Commissioners.
Referred to the Committee of the Whole.
8. The Mayor respectfully requested acceptance of a Special Act regarding Health Insurance 
for the Mayor. President Logan explained that this communication is substantially the 
same as a matter which is currently pending before the Ordinances and Rules Committee 
(that matter being the communication from the Mayor dated 5/20/2024 entitled Special 
Act – Healthcare for Mayor) and therefore in accordance with Council Rule 30, this may 
not be accepted as a new matter. Therefore, this communication will be accepted as 
informational communication under Rule 58 and the Clerk is directed to attach this 
Communication to the matter already in committee. 
9. The Mayor respectfully requested your guidance about a naming request from Margaret 
Cannon related to 617 Lexington St and former Superintendent John Daddona. The mayor 
respectfully requests an answer from the Council. Referred to the Licenses and Franchises 
Committee.
10. The Mayor respectfully requested acceptance of two taking orders for the easements 
necessary to finish the traffic project on Pelham Road. Referred to the Committee of the 
Whole.
3
11. The Mayor respectfully requested a funding transfer totaling $1,158,400 to fund the first 
year and second year of a three-year amendment to the Non-Union Compensation 
Ordinance covering the period July 1,2025 to June 30, 2028. Referred to the Finance 
Committee.
12. The Mayor respectfully requested adoption of the compensation ordinance to amend the 
existing pay charts for non-union employees. Referred to the Ordinances and Rules 
Committee.
13. The Mayor respectfully requested a transfer in the amount of $11,809.14 to purchase 
survey equipment for the in-house survey work that is performed by the Engineering 
Department Staff. Referred to the Finance Committee.
14. The Mayor respectfully requested a transfer of funds in the amount of $32,000 for the 
design services that were not included in the original scope of work for the Beaver Street 
railroad crossing project. Referred to the Finance Committee.
15. The Mayor respectfully requested approval of a financing transaction in the total amount 
of $3,717,000 for a water/sewer/street infrastructure project for Bolton, Caughey, Clinton, 
Cutter, Day, Graymore and Mt. Pleasants Streets. Referred to the Finance Committee.
16. The Mayor respectfully requested approval of a loan authorization for the purchase and 
installation of a new Zetron Max station alerting and radio control system for the 911 
Dispatch Center. Referred to the Finance Committee.
17. The Mayor respectfully requested an opportunity to go into Executive Session regarding 
the purchase of 14-16 Spring Street, Waltham. Referred to the Committee of the Whole.
18. The Mayor respectfully requested an opportunity to go into Executive Session regarding 
the purchase of 600 Main Street. Referred to the Committee of the Whole.
Applications and Licenses
All Applications and Licenses referred to the Licenses and Franchises Committee.
